all_rows.paragraph: \textbf{Synchrotron radiation.} In the presence of the Galactic magnetic field ($B \sim$ few $\mu$G), ultra-relativistic electrons gyrate around magnetic field lines and emit synchrotron radiation. This process primarily generates photons in the radio and microwave bands, but it traces the same underlying electron populations that produce gamma rays via ICS and bremsstrahlung. The synchrotron energy loss rate scales as $b_\text{syn} \propto B^2 E_e^2$ \cite{Hooper:2024}, mirroring the $E_e^2$ dependence of Thomson-regime ICS.
